findings.origin: derived from audit, NOT an original task ID
findings.issue: Unpaired Unicode surrogates and oversized UTF-8 strings escaped the typed evidence boundary.
findings.implemented_behavior: Reject invalid scalar strings/keys and byte budgets before serialization; retain Hindi/emoji and valid surrogate pairs.
findings.boundaries: Unicode/byte limits are defensive input checks, not source truth or text semantics.

findings.origin: derived from audit, NOT an original task ID
findings.issue: Registry unconditionally used a Python3.12-only SQLite keyword despite the advertised3.11 minimum; lexical parent symlinks were not centrally guarded.
findings.implemented_behavior: Use explicit manual transactions with version-aware connection parameters and reject symlink/URI/traversal paths.
findings.boundaries: Executed on Python3.13.5;3.11 API behavior is simulated, not an actual3.11 platform run. Single-owner preflight is not race-proof OS containment.

findings.origin: derived from audit, NOT an original task ID
findings.issue: Unexpected metric errors escaped; a malformed/misbound/overcredited result could escape or be represented incorrectly.
findings.implemented_behavior: Freeze evaluator inputs; validate context pins, unit-weighted scores and receipt construction inside one fail-closed boundary; redact exception details.
findings.boundaries: Bounded deterministic profiles still do not judge arbitrary language or guarantee scientific truth. Re-audit malformed-result failures and fixes are retained.

findings.implemented_behavior: Use detached request-bound snapshots and recheck provider/model/fixture identity after execution.
findings.boundaries: No live provider is selected or called. An in-process adapter is still trusted operator code; use the supervised wrapper for a hard deadline.

findings.origin: derived from audit, NOT an original task ID
findings.issue: The model port delegated timeouts to the adapter; a hanging callback had no enforced process deadline.
findings.implemented_behavior: Offer an operator-installed factory wrapper with spawned worker, bounded UTF-8 response channel, deadline termination and direct-child reaping.
findings.boundaries: Not an OS sandbox: descendant, network, memory, service authorization and provider billing cancellation remain deployment concerns. Wrapper adoption by the native broker is not automatic.

findings.origin: derived from audit, NOT an original task ID
findings.issue: A content-hashed assessment could self-assert a production execution identity without a per-assessment service authorization.
findings.implemented_behavior: Require exact signed assessment scopes, configured roles/identity/version/group, expiry/revocation, non-fixture execution and no reused secret across raters.
findings.boundaries: Configured shared-secret service custody is not independent digital non-repudiation, actual reviewer expertise, honest external evidence or protected production key provisioning.

findings.origin: derived from audit, NOT an original task ID
findings.issue: Global metric and domain aggregates could conceal missing domain-by-metric cells; the hardened gate inputs also needed CLI wiring.
findings.implemented_behavior: Pin an exact full17-metric roster per domain; require independent reference/leakage-group components per cell; bind the contract into external attestation scope and expose all required inputs through the CLI.
findings.boundaries: No automatic not-applicable exemptions and no empirical calibration claimed. Synthetic full-matrix controls use invented evidence and test signing identities, not a real production/golden approval.

findings.origin: derived from audit, NOT an original task ID
findings.issue: A finalization could return a receipt without ensuring its reserved row was finalized; interrupted reservations lacked a governed terminal recovery path.
findings.implemented_behavior: Compare-and-set finalization, read-back integrity, artifact/report bindings and explicit input-pinned operator recovery to terminal BLOCKED.
findings.boundaries: Single-host privileged recovery requires stopping the abandoned worker first. It is not an authenticated public recovery endpoint or distributed crash reconciliation. Pre-H1 finalized receipts require explicit revalidation; do not rewrite archived evidence.

findings.origin: derived from audit, NOT an original task ID
findings.issue: Resolving paths before checking them hid root/parent symlinks; normalized Unicode/Windows aliases were not rejected. An inherited preservation assertion needed a tracked-change path rather than a skip.
findings.implemented_behavior: Reject lexical symlink roots/parents and nonportable aliases, verify exact inventories, and require original preimages plus old/new hashes for intentional baseline replacements.
findings.boundaries: Extraction remains for trusted operator-owned parents, not hostile concurrent filesystem writers. Historical original archives remain byte-identical; one old test file is deliberately updated and preserved.
